transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you, too. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, and please let me know if I'm not giving you what you need, but... I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. I’ve always been a bit of a busy guy, which is usually a good thing, right? Being productive and all that. I just can't really idle very well. 

But, well, we recently got a new work setup at my job—I do customer service—and it's just... it's made it a lot harder to hide the fact that I need to keep moving. It's really nothing too terrible, I just thought I should maybe get it checked out. Does that make sense?
When you feel this need to keep moving, do you experience it as a physical restlessness, or is it more of a mental feeling of being worried or anxious about things?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I don't think it's a worried feeling, really. I'm not usually an anxious guy. It's more of a... a physical thing, I guess? 

Like, if I have to sit still through a long training video for work, or if I'm stuck in a really slow appointment, I just start to feel kind of... boxed in? I hope that makes sense. It's nothing extreme, I just get this feeling like I really need to stand up, or stretch, or at least do something with my hands. Just to stay alert, I suppose. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Looking back at your childhood—say, in elementary or middle school—did you often have trouble sitting still in class or focusing on your schoolwork?

Oh, wow, going way back... well, yes, I suppose so. I mean, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I really did respect my teachers—but I guess this feeling has been around long before the new job setup. 

Back in grade school, my report cards usually said I was a bright student, which was always nice to hear! But... well, they also tended to say I was a little careless. And I guess they mentioned that I talked out of turn sometimes, or had to be reminded to stay with my work. I think I was just a bit too chatty and eager to participate, you know? Just a typical energetic boy, I always figured. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it was, I wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything. 

Does that... does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
When you have a project or a series of tasks to complete, do you find that you struggle to keep things organized or have trouble finishing what you started?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best to stay on top of everything, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job well... but, I guess sometimes, yes, that can happen a little bit. 

Like, if a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation at work, I'm always really eager to jump right in and help. I'll usually do the first part right away, but then... well, somehow I might accidentally leave the notes or the follow-up part sitting there unfinished. Just until someone reminds me, of course! Once they mention it, I get it done right away. 

It's really not that I'm trying to slack off or ignore the instructions, I just sort of... lose track of the last few steps once the main problem is handled, I guess? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible employee. Is that... is that the kind of example you were looking for?

Outside of your work and your school days, do you find that this tendency to lose track of details or struggle to finish tasks also affects your personal life, such as with household chores or managing your daily errands?

Oh, um... well, at home, I guess I'm pretty much the same way. I really do try to keep on top of things, though! I'm not, you know, living in a mess or anything like that. 

But, um... well, I suppose it happens with the little things. Like, even at work, I'll fully intend to call a customer back, or maybe reply to an internal message right after my lunch break. I really mean to do it! But... if I don't write it down—and I usually have to write it in more than one place just to be safe—it might just sort of... slip my mind completely until the next day. 

I always feel terrible when it happens, and I always apologize and fix it right away. It's just that my brain gets so busy with the next thing, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound completely unreliable. Does that make sense? Is that what you meant by everyday things?
In your daily conversations with friends or colleagues, do you find that you often interrupt others or finish their sentences before they've finished speaking?

Oh, gosh, that's a tough one. Um... I really pride myself on being a team player, and I'd hate for anyone to think I'm being rude or overstepping. I always try to be respectful of everyone's space and time. 

But, well... I suppose sometimes I do get a little ahead of myself. Like, if I'm at my desk and I overhear some of my coworkers trying to figure out a tricky customer problem... I just want to help so badly! So, I might accidentally just... jump right in and give them the answer before they've even finished explaining it to each other, or, you know, before anyone actually asked for my input. 

I really just want to save them time and be helpful, I promise! I don't mean to intrude or cut them off. I just get so excited when I know the solution and want to share it right away. I always apologize if I startled them. Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a know-it-all or anything.

When you are working on a task that requires sustained mental effort, such as reading a long document or completing detailed paperwork, do you find that you often make careless mistakes or lose your focus because your mind wanders?

Oh, um... well, I really try to be as careful as possible, especially with paperwork. I know how important it is to get all those details right, and I always want to make sure I'm doing a good job for the customers and the company. 

But... I guess sometimes, if it's a really long ticket or there are a lot of tiny little steps, my mind might wander just a tiny bit. It's not that I'm not trying to pay attention! It's just... well, sometimes I'll think I've completely finished a customer ticket and done everything perfectly. But then, maybe later on, I'll realize I accidentally typed one wrong digit in the account number, or maybe I just skipped past one little required box by mistake. Or I might miss one tiny instruction, and then the whole ticket comes back to me to fix. 

I always feel so embarrassed when that happens, and I fix it immediately, of course! I just... I think sometimes my brain is already moving on to the next customer who needs help before my hands have finished with the first one. I really hope that doesn't make me sound careless. I do try my very best to catch those things. Is that... is that the kind of mistake you meant?

Looking back at your life, would you say that the challenges with focus and organization have been more frequent and persistent for you than the physical restlessness and the tendency to interrupt others?

Oh, um... gosh, comparing them like that is a bit tricky. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm struggling all the time with either of them, you know? I try so hard to keep everything balanced and to be a good employee and a good person to be around. 

But... well, if I really have to think about which one has been around more... I'm honestly not entirely sure. I mean, I try to keep the fidgeting under control, and I definitely try my hardest not to interrupt anyone! And I do my best to stay organized, too. I guess... I guess maybe they just sort of happen together? Or maybe I just haven't paid close enough attention to which one is worse. I really hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want to exaggerate one over the other if I'm not completely certain. Does that make sense? I'm sorry I can't give you a more definitive answer on that one.
If you had to choose, would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and organized happen more often than your physical restlessness and tendency to jump into conversations?

Oh, um... you're asking me that again. I'm sorry, I must not have been very clear before. I really don't want to be difficult, I promise. 

It's just... I honestly don't know if I can pick one over the other. I mean, I really try to be mindful of both, you know? I want to be someone who pays attention to detail, and I certainly don't want to be the guy who can't sit still or who talks over people. 

So, I guess... I really just haven't noticed one being more of a problem than the other. They both just sort of... pop up now and then, despite my best efforts. I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you're looking for. I just don't want to give you the wrong impression or make it sound worse than it is. Is it okay that I'm just not sure?

When you were a child, did you find that these difficulties with sitting still or staying focused were present in places other than school, such as at home or when you were out with friends or family?

Oh, um... childhood... gosh, that's going back a bit. I really try to just focus on the positive memories, you know? I had a nice childhood, and my parents were wonderful. 

But, um... as for whether those things happened at home or with friends... I honestly don't remember it being a big issue outside of school. I mean, maybe I was a little energetic, like any kid? But I always tried to be good for my parents and polite when we went out. I don't think I was a terror at the dinner table or anything like that! 

I really don't recall my parents or my friends' parents ever being terribly upset with me. I always wanted to make sure everyone was happy. So, I don't think it was a problem everywhere, if that makes sense? I hope that's a helpful answer. I just don't want to paint myself as having been a really difficult child when I don't think I was. Is that... does that sound like what you're asking?
When you were a child, can you recall any specific times, perhaps during family gatherings or playdates, where your parents or other adults had to ask you to slow down or pay more attention?

Oh, um... well, I guess if I really think about it... I mean, I try not to dwell on the negative things, but... well, I suppose it's been around for a long time, long before I started my current job. 

I do remember... well, my parents were always so supportive, but I think in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright—which was nice of them to say!—but they'd also mention that I could be a little careless sometimes. And, um, they did say I talked out of turn occasionally and had to be reminded to stay on task with my work. 

I really tried my best to be a good student, I promise! I just... I guess I got a little distracted or excited sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid. I always wanted to do well and make my teachers happy. Does that help answer your question? I'm sorry if it's not exactly what you were looking for.
Looking back at your childhood, can you remember if you had these same difficulties with staying focused or sitting still when you were at home or with friends, rather than just at school?

Oh, um... you know, I think we might have just touched on that a moment ago? I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear enough the first time—I really don't want to make you repeat yourself. 

But yes, like I was saying, I honestly don't remember it being much of an issue at home or when I was just hanging out with friends. My parents never seemed too worried, and I always tried to be on my best behavior for them. I really wanted to be a good kid, you know? I'd help out around the house and try to be polite when we had company. 

So, outside of school, I don't think anyone really saw me as someone who couldn't sit still or pay attention. I was just... well, just a normal boy, I think? I hope that's okay. I really don't want to give you the wrong idea about how I was raised or anything. Is that... does that cover what you were asking?

When you think back to your childhood, were there any times at home or with friends where you were told that you were being too loud, moving around too much, or not paying enough attention to what was going on?

Oh, my... I feel just awful, I feel like I'm frustrating you because we keep coming back to this, and I really don't want to be a difficult patient! I'm so sorry if my answers aren't quite what you need. 

But, um... honestly, no. I really can't think of any times like that at home or with my buddies. I always tried to be very respectful. I mean, if we were outside playing, maybe we were a little loud just because we were young boys having fun? But I don't remember ever being scolded by my parents or anyone else for moving around too much or ignoring people. I always made sure I was listening when adults spoke to me, because it was really important to me to be polite and stay out of trouble. 

I'm so sorry, I really wish I had a better example for you. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not messing up your assessment.

In your current life, at home, do you find that you frequently lose important items like your keys, wallet, or phone, or have trouble keeping your living space tidy because of these difficulties with focus?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I think I'm pretty good about keeping track of my things. I always try to put my keys in the same little bowl by the door, and my wallet usually stays in my pocket or on the nightstand. I mean, sure, maybe once in a great while I'll misplace my phone for a minute or two, but doesn't everyone do that sometimes? I don't think it's anything out of the ordinary.

And as for my place... well, I try my best to keep it neat. I really don't like living in a mess. It might get a little cluttered if I've had a long week at work and haven't had time to put everything away perfectly, but I always make sure it's clean enough if anyone comes over. I really try to stay on top of it. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely disorganized or anything like that. I really do try hard to keep things nice and tidy. Is that okay?
Do you feel that these challenges with focus, restlessness, or impulsivity have significantly interfered with your ability to perform your job duties or maintain your personal relationships?

Oh, um... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or anything, because I really do try my best. I mean, my personal relationships are fine, I think! I get along really well with people. 

But, um... at work... I guess it has been coming up a little bit lately. I work in customer service, and I'm really good with the customers, I promise! They always say I'm very polite. But... well, in my recent reviews, my supervisors have started pointing out a few things. Just, you know, some unfinished tickets and... and a few little mistakes here and there. They said it kind of slows the team down sometimes. 

I felt just terrible when they told me that. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone, and I'm trying so hard to keep up. I just get a little side-tracked sometimes, I suppose. Is... is it normal to struggle with that kind of thing? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job. I hope that doesn't make you think poorly of my work ethic.

Looking back at your childhood, can you recall any specific situations outside of school, such as at home or during extracurricular activities, where you were told you needed to be less active or more attentive?

Oh, gosh... I know I just said I didn't remember anything like that at home, and I really hope you don't think I was lying to you! I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, but it's a little embarrassing to admit. 

I guess... well, if I really think about it, these issues didn't just start with my recent job troubles. I remember back in grade school... my teachers, they were always very nice, but they used to write on my report cards that I was, um, bright but... careless. And that I talked out of turn sometimes. They'd say I had to be reminded to stay with my work. 

I feel awful even saying it now, because I really did try to be a good student! I just... I don't want you to think I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I was just a little overly enthusiastic, maybe? Is it okay that I'm telling you this now? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
